no timeout, no cancel anywhere. A 5s saturated UART capture spends 6.9s inside one un-interruptible runPython call. libsigrokdecode ships srd_session_terminate_reset and Pyodide ships setInterruptBuffer; neither is used

32-bit sample ceiling undocumented: Int32Array throughout means 2^31 samples, which at this device's 200 MSa/s is a 10.7 SECOND capture

All three hwcaptures open, and an independent 8N1 framer in the suite recovers the generator's 'Hello' from uart.sr's D9 - the whole zip->edges path is known-answer-proven. 12/12, mutation-checked

gap parity corruption fixed: saveLwcap and RleSampleStore.fromStore rebuilt channels from the gap-filtered edges(), so a gap swallowing an ODD number of edges inverted every level from the gap's end to the end of the capture - on known data the source store had right. Both now go through channelAcrossGaps (src/data/gaps.ts): ask the source store for the level at each gap's end, insert one synthetic edge at endSample-1 when the filtered list disagrees. MEASURED before: channels 1 and 2 (odd counts) inverted, the other 14 (even) did not; after: 0/2 and 0/14. Mutation-checked both ways - neutering the fixup turns both suites red, and placing the edge at endSample instead throws 'edges are not strictly increasing' because a real edge already sits there. Why it survived two rounds: both suites guarded with c1 <= G0 AND the data suite's channel list [0,5,12,15] had zero overlap with the odd-parity channels [1,2,11], so removing the guard alone left it green

throughput measured at every capture width, not just 16 ch. The three advertised ceilings (4x800, 8x400, 16x200 MS/s) are one 400 MB/s wire budget divided by the bit width, and the device holds it at all three: 399.4 / 398.3 / 399.5 MB/s, zero short transfers. PREDICTION FALSIFIED: I predicted 4ch@800MHz would fall short because expandPacked must unpack 400 MB/s of wire into 800 MB/s in a scalar JS loop. It does not - sink/raw is exactly 2.0000, so the loop really delivered 2.39 GB in 3.0 s = 799 MB/s. I asserted a cost was prohibitive without computing it (~5 cycles/iteration at 4 GHz). device/NOTES.md P3 records the identical error, so this is the second time; logged as P5. Still no WebUSB ceiling in evidence

dropout consumer wired (appendLostSamples in src/data/gaps.ts). It was dead for two rounds and the cause was structural, not a bad guard: with no samples appended the lost span has zero width in store coordinates, so there was nothing for noteGap to mark. Decision taken - append filler for the lost samples so the store's axis keeps tracking device time. The filler repeats the LAST KNOWN SAMPLE rather than zeroing; zeros invent a rising edge at the gap's end, which sits outside the gap where edges() reports it as real (MEASURED: exactly 16 spurious edges, 1 per channel). Pinned end to end in offline-test.ts: 383948 delivered + 50 lost = store length 383998, one gap at [255948, 255998). Mutation-checked both ways - zeroed filler turns the edge check red, skipping the append throws 'gap [255948,255998) outside 0 <= start < end <= 255948', which is the zero-width problem stating itself. Lost-sample count now shows in the capture panel while recording. Hardware has still never produced a short transfer, so this runs only against the scripted device
